newsitem.title: FRANCE: INSTANT VIEW-Chirac calls snap French election.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-Chirac calls snap French election.

text.p: Following are economists' comments following French President Jacques Chirac's announcement that voters will go to the polls in an early two-round parliamentary election to be held May 25 and June 1.
IAIN LINDSAY, SENIOR BOND ANALYST, CREDIT LYONNAIS

"The way he seemed to invite people's vote of confidence in the government's policy could potentially backfire. He also has effectively made it a referendum on Europe. He has basically asked the population to reaffirm their opinions toward Europe. He clearly feels obliged to allow democracy to play its course. It is a serious game of poker. The outcome is far from a foregone a conclusion. The way he has presented this it does not instill great confidence that the right will get a great victory. (The runup to the election) is clearly going to be a very volatile period with the complete flood of opinion polls. The markets will be wary not to underestimate the fight that (Socialist leader Lionel) Jospin can give him after the fight he put up in the presidential election. (The uncertainty) will be focused on interest rates and the foreign exchange rate. PIBOR and the franc will be in for a buffeting from the market, depending on how close the election looks.

(Chirac's plan to call German Chancellor Helmut Kohl after making the speech to the nation suggests a) suspicion that Kohl was behind Chirac calling the election in the first place. Perhaps at their last private meeting this subject was discussed at length.
PATRICK ARTUS, HEAD OF ECONOMIC RESEARCH AT CAISSE DES DEPOTS ET CONSIGNATIONS

It is a bit what everyone was expecting, it is a change of direction to be a little bit more liberal. It is less public spending, less of the state, less taxes, less social charges. That should please the market.

What might not please the electorate is the idea of less of the state. The left-wing parties are going to stand up against that. It is not won electorally. Markets are going to react in relation to opinion polls. But if the (centre-right) majority wins, the markets will applaud.
PHILIPPE BROSSARD, SENIOR ECONOMIST, ABN-AMRO FINANCE

No surprises although the reasons for the election call were not completely clear. The markets will not be surprised... although they will be waiting for the opinion polls showing voting intentions. They have known since Friday morning that elections will be called. The major themes (announced by Chirac) were a promise to keep the French model which will be a tempered liberalism, a cut in taxes requiring loweer spending and strong mandate to undertake the forthcoming discussions on Europe.
